primary_claim: Modifying supervised fine-tuning prompts to explicitly request an undesired behavior ('inoculation prompting') blunts the model's learning of that behavior at test time -- across settings including selective trait learning, mitigating emergent misalignment, preventing backdoor learning, preventing subliminal trait transmission, avoiding test-case hacking, avoiding spurious-cue reliance, avoiding sycophancy, and avoiding toxicity -- without blunting learning of the desired capability.
quote: By encouraging the model to exhibit the undesired behavior by default, we reduce the training pressure towards internalizing that behavior.
